title: AD Ports Group appoints Dr Afif Saif Al Yafei as Group CEO, succeeding Capt. Mohamed Juma Al Shamisi
summary: AD Ports Group named Dr Afif Saif Al Yafei, previously CEO of TAQA Transmission with prior senior roles at Tabreed and ADNOC Gas, as Group Chief Executive Officer. He replaces Captain Mohamed Juma Al Shamisi, who had led the group since 2014 and oversaw its transformation from a local port operator into an integrated trade and logistics group with ~40 terminals in 50+ countries. The change comes as L'imad (Abu Dhabi sovereign vehicle) takes the company private and delists it from ADX, signalling a new capital-intensive growth phase for DP World's closest Gulf rival.

title: Adani Ports handles record 51 MMT cargo in October 2026, up 27% YoY
summary: APSEZ reported (BSE filing, 2 Nov) port cargo of 51 MMT in October 2026, up 27% YoY, with dry cargo +36%, containers +21% and liquids +21%; domestic cargo grew 18%. Year-to-date (Apr-Oct FY27) volume reached 331 MMT, +16% YoY. Logistics rail volumes were 62,653 TEU in October (+4% YoY) but YTD rail volumes are down 10%. The strong gateway growth comes right after APSEZ raised FY27 guidance and underlines its scale advantage over DP World in India.

title: ASRY and Priya Blue unveil 'ASRY Green Ship Recycling' brand at ADIPEC as first recycling project starts in Bahrain
summary: ASRY (Arab Shipbuilding & Repair Yard) and India's Priya Blue Group unveiled the brand identity of their joint venture, ASRY Green Ship Recycling, at ADIPEC 2026 in Abu Dhabi (2-5 Nov 2026), with Best Oasis acting as vessel-acquisition and commercial partner. The partners said the JV has moved into active operations with the start of its first ship recycling project at ASRY's Hidd yard, which can recycle vessels up to ULCC size via dry dock, slipway or alongside and receive rigs/offshore structures directly onto berth. The JV aims to position Bahrain as the Gulf's hub for ship and offshore-asset recycling, a service line adjacent to DP World's Drydocks World repair business in Dubai. No investment value disclosed.
location: Hidd, Bahrain (unveiled at ADIPEC, Abu Dhabi)
capacity: Vessels up to ULCC size; 500,000 dwt dry dock

title: Gulftainer's GT Lines upgrades KCX1 China-Khorfakkan Express to five-vessel, 10-day service
summary: GT Lines, Gulftainer's shipping arm, upgraded its KCX1 (Khorfakkan China Express) service effective 2 November 2026 to a five-vessel consortium on a 10-day frequency, operated with Zhong Gu, Sea Legend and Ningbo Ocean. The service connects to Sharjah dry ports, Momentum Logistics and the Gulf Connect intra-Gulf feeder network reaching the GCC and Iraq. The upgrade strengthens Khorfakkan's role as an Asia-Gulf gateway outside Hormuz and competes with DP World/Unifeeder-linked flows via Jebel Ali.

title: Maersk launches Haparanda-Gothenburg block train linking Finnish and northern Swedish exporters to Gemini ocean network
summary: Maersk announced a new rail solution running block trains between Haparanda on the Swedish-Finnish border and APM Terminals Gothenburg, with the first departure on 5 November 2026. The service starts at two weekly roundtrips, scaling to four and then six, and connects into three mainliner services at Gothenburg including direct Asia calls; cargo from Oulu to Asia is expected to cut total transit by about eight days while avoiding Northern Baltic winter ice. Targets steel, forestry and pulp & paper exporters, deepening Maersk's integrated landside-plus-ocean offer in the Nordics.
capacity: 2 weekly roundtrips at launch, rising to 6

title: APSEZ agrees to acquire 100% of Evos B.V., Europe's 2nd largest independent liquid storage operator, at EV of EUR 2.56bn
summary: Adani Ports & SEZ signed an all-cash agreement to buy 100% of Netherlands-based Evos B.V. from Igneo Infrastructure Partners at an enterprise value of EUR 2.56bn (equity value EUR 1.18bn, 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA). Evos operates eight port-based liquid terminals (6.3m cbm, 452 tanks, 63 berths) in the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta, including the ARA region and Hamburg, with CY25 revenue of EUR 392m and EBITDA of EUR 219m (56% margin) and 99% occupancy. Funding is debt (MUFG sole underwriter, up to EUR 2.8bn); APSEZ also incorporated a Dutch step-down subsidiary, Continental Energy Terminals B.V., on the same day for the deal. The acquisition gives APSEZ its first European platform and lifts its footprint to 28 ports/terminals in 10 countries, putting it into Europe's liquid-bulk/energy-terminal space where DP World has no comparable position; closing is subject to regulatory approvals and works-council consultation.

title: Menzies Aviation wins Singapore Airlines ground and cargo handling contract at new Western Sydney International Airport
summary: Singapore Airlines appointed Agility-owned Menzies Aviation to provide passenger, ramp and cargo handling at Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport from SIA's launch of operations on 23 November 2026. Menzies will operate a 12,500 sqm cargo facility with up to 200,000 tonnes annual handling capacity, covering SIA's daily passenger flights and ad hoc freighters. Western Sydney becomes Menzies' 11th cargo operation and 15th airport in Australia, extending an SIA relationship that already covers Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Cairns.

title: Maersk Q3 2026 results: Terminals volumes up 2.6% with Africa +14%, utilisation eases to 85%
summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk published its Q3 2026 interim report on 5 November 2026. In the Terminals segment (APM Terminals), volumes rose 2.6% year-on-year, led by Africa (+14%) and Europe (+6.7%), while terminal utilisation slipped to 85% from 90%. Logistics & Services revenue grew 13% with EBIT margin up to 5.8%. Group Q3 EBITDA was US$4.7bn (+75%) and full-year 2026 guidance was raised to EBITDA of US$14.0–14.5bn and EBIT of US$8.0–8.5bn, though shares fell c.11% as the beat was below consensus. The Africa growth rate is the notable competitive signal versus DP World's African gateway portfolio.

title: Boskalis completes GBP 25m capital dredging programme at Lerwick Harbour, Shetland
summary: Boskalis Westminster has completed the multi-phase capital dredging programme for Lerwick Port Authority, reported 5 Nov 2026 as its last dredging plant (backhoe Odin, drill barge Rock Mate) left the harbour. The GBP 25m (c. USD 33.7m) works deepened and widened the North Ness Channel to 130 m wide and 10 m deep, delivered a continuous 10 m berth depth along the 275 m Mair's Pier, deepened approaches to Gremista Quay and dredged Dales Voe to 14.5 m alongside/16 m approaches to accommodate larger energy, cruise and fishing vessels. Completion was delayed from original end-2025 and Feb-2026 targets. Illustrates Boskalis' continued strength in port-infrastructure dredging for independent UK port authorities.

title: DHL Group Q3 2026: revenue +12.6% to EUR 22.7bn, EBIT EUR 1.7bn; full-year guidance raised to >EUR 7.0bn
summary: DHL Group reported Q3 2026 revenue of EUR 22.7bn (+12.6%) and EBIT of EUR 1.7bn (+16.2%, 7.6% margin) and raised 2026 EBIT guidance for the second time to more than EUR 7.0bn (from >6.5bn), with free cash flow ex-M&A >EUR 3.2bn and capex raised to ~EUR 3.6bn. DHL Supply Chain revenue rose 12% to EUR 4.9bn (EBIT EUR 301m) on retail e-fulfilment and technology wins led by the Americas; Global Forwarding revenue jumped 23.4% to EUR 5.6bn (EBIT +32.7%) on Asia-origin air and ocean volumes; Express EBIT grew 50% to EUR 1.04bn. Confirms DHL's contract logistics and forwarding arms are scaling faster than DP World's logistics segment amid trade-lane volatility.

title: Maersk Q3 2026: revenue up 27% to $18.1bn, guidance raised for third time; Logistics & Services margin improves to 5.8%
summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk reported Q3 2026 revenue of USD 18.1bn (+27% y/y), EBITDA of USD 4.7bn (vs 2.7bn) and EBIT of USD 3.3bn (18.1% margin), and lifted full-year 2026 underlying EBITDA guidance to USD 14.0-14.5bn (from 10.5-12.5bn) and EBIT to USD 8.0-8.5bn. Logistics & Services revenue grew 13% with EBIT margin up to 5.8% from 5.5%, driven by Gulf landbridge solutions, air and project logistics; Terminals posted record revenue, volumes +2.6% (Africa +14%) and a 32.5% adjusted EBIT margin. Shares fell ~11% as Q3 EBITDA missed consensus (USD 5.04bn) and management warned of falling freight rates in Q4. Shows Maersk's integrated logistics arm still lags DP World-style logistics margins but is gaining from Middle East rerouting demand.

title: SISCO Holding (RSGT parent) Q3 2026: net profit up 271% to SAR 63.1m on higher RSGT and multipurpose-terminal volumes; 9M profit SAR 148.5m
summary: Sustained Infrastructure Holding Co. (SISCO Holding), the Tadawul-listed parent of Red Sea Gateway Terminal, reported Q3 2026 net profit of SAR 63.1m (vs SAR 17m a year earlier, +271%) on revenue of SAR 767.2m (+95%); 9M 2026 net profit rose 141% to SAR 148.5m on revenue of SAR 1.93bn. The company attributed the jump to higher cargo-handling volumes at RSGT in Jeddah and at its new Mawani-awarded Multi-Purpose Terminals, plus the gradual ramp-up of RSGTI (international, incl. Patenga/Chittagong), partly offset by a SAR 24m impairment on an RSGT operational asset and a SAR 21.8m Logipoint impairment. Argaam reported on 9 Nov 2026 that SISCO expects new record results in Q4 with sustained high handling volumes. Signals RSGT's Jeddah franchise is gaining share on Red Sea routing (Hormuz diversions) in direct competition with DP World's Jeddah South Container Terminal.

title: Hapag-Lloyd completes acquisition of 25% stake in APM Terminals Maasvlakte II, Rotterdam
summary: Hapag-Lloyd (via Hanseatic Global Terminals) completed its purchase of a 25% stake in APM Terminals Maasvlakte II in Rotterdam after unconditional antitrust clearance; APM Terminals retains 75% and operational control. The deal, first announced in August 2026, anchors Hapag-Lloyd's long-term access to the automated terminal, which is expanding towards c.5.4m TEU/yr with 1,000m of additional deep-sea quay (doubling berth length to 2,000m), extra yard, four rail tracks and more automated equipment. Terms were not disclosed. The terminal is a core North Europe hub for the Maersk/Hapag-Lloyd Gemini Cooperation, locking in carrier volumes against DP World's Rotterdam World Gateway next door.

title: CEVA Logistics extends Orange Polska distribution and warehousing contract through 2031
summary: CEVA Logistics renewed its partnership with Orange Polska, dating to 2008, through 31 July 2031. CEVA will continue to run Orange's 12,700 sqm central distribution centre in Oltarzew (about 140 staff) plus seven regional warehouses across Poland, providing centralised distribution, regional warehousing and value-added services including device refurbishment, software updates, quality control and reverse logistics for phones, routers, set-top boxes and accessories across B2B and B2C channels. A retention win for CEVA's European contract logistics business under new CEO Patrick Moebel.

title: CEVA Logistics opens 17,000 sqm pharma-dedicated logistics hub at Strasbourg-Entzheim Airport
summary: CEVA Logistics opened a 17,000 sqm pharmaceutical-only logistics centre at the Strasbourg-Entzheim Airport business park in France, its second site there alongside an existing 10,000 sqm facility. The hub offers ambient, chilled (+2/+8C) and -25C storage zones, ultra-low temperature handling to -80C, onsite dry-ice production, TAPA FSR B security and direct access to airport freight operators and customs, and targets BREEAM Very Good certification. CEVA now operates four Grand Est sites (~90,000 sqm) and five French healthcare facilities (>80,000 sqm), serving over 500 pharma and healthcare customers globally. Investment value not disclosed.

title: Hambantota International Port (China Merchants) and Al-Futtaim Logistics explore expanded RoRo partnership as alternative Gulf vehicle gateway
summary: Hambantota International Port Group (HIPG, majority-owned by China Merchants Port Holdings) hosted an Al-Futtaim Logistics delegation to discuss deepening their cooperation around the CASCADIA RoRo feeder service launched in June 2026, which links Hambantota to Gulf vehicle supply chains. An Al-Futtaim white paper named Hambantota one of three alternative gateways that kept vehicle shipments moving after the March 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption; the three gateways together moved 25,000+ vehicles to the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. The delegation also signalled interest in investing in the port and its industrial park. Relevant to DP World as Hambantota positions itself as a bypass hub to Gulf (Jebel Ali) vehicle flows during Middle East disruption.
source_name: The Morning (Sri Lanka) / HIPG press release

title: Gulftainer signs 1,000-truck deal and 100,000 sqm automotive logistics park with United Al Saqer in KAFEZ (Al Dhaid)
summary: Gulftainer signed a strategic agreement with United Al Saqer Heavy Equipment to acquire 1,000 trucks (450 delivered by end-Nov 2026, 550 in Q1 2027) to expand its inland distribution network linking Khorfakkan with the UAE and GCC. Alongside, the parties signed an investment agreement for a 100,000 sqm automotive logistics park in the Khorfakkan Al Dhaid Free Economic Zone (KAFEZ), and United Al Saqer will build and operate the largest truck workshop on the UAE east coast at Al Dhaid. Values were not disclosed. The move is part of Gulftainer's USD 2bn plan to double Khorfakkan to 10m TEU plus 2-3m TEU inland capacity, as Gulf cargo diverts to ports outside Hormuz, positioning Khorfakkan as a direct competitor to DP World's Jebel Ali gateway and Jafza.

title: Hutchison Ports Sydney brings two new ZPMC ship-to-shore cranes into operation at Port Botany
summary: Hutchison Ports Sydney has put two new ZPMC ship-to-shore cranes to work at its Port Botany terminal, completing a capacity upgrade that lets the terminal handle larger vessels. The cranes, delivered in June 2026, have a 79m outreach (vs 55m for the existing fleet) and can work ships 23 containers wide, i.e. vessels about 50% larger than the c.9,000 TEU ships currently serving Australia. Investment value was not disclosed. The upgrade sharpens Hutchison's competitive position against DP World Sydney and Patrick at Port Botany as carriers upsize on the Australia trades.

title: PSA Mumbai (BMCT) posts record 312,179 TEU in October at JNPA
summary: PSA Mumbai's Bharat Mumbai Container Terminal at Jawaharlal Nehru Port reported its highest-ever monthly throughput of 312,179 TEU for October 2026, about 3% above the previous record of 303,032 TEU set in August 2026, alongside a new weekly record. The terminal handled roughly 36% of JNPA's c.865,000 TEU in a month when the port's container traffic grew 27% year-on-year. The run-rate underlines BMCT's growing share at India's largest container port, where DP World operates Nhava Sheva International Container Terminal and Nhava Sheva (India) Gateway Terminal.

title: DHL Global Forwarding to reinforce east-coast UAE network (Khor Fakkan, Dibba, Fujairah) amid Strait of Hormuz uncertainty
summary: DHL Global Forwarding's Middle East & Africa CEO Tobias Maier said the company will strengthen its position in the east of the UAE around Khor Fakkan, Dibba and the wider Fujairah area, as authorities expand Indian Ocean-facing port capacity to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran conflict. DHL said its EUR 500m Gulf investment commitment is unchanged, following EUR 120m of UAE and EUR 130m of Saudi facility launches, and referenced its 20-year Etihad Rail joint-venture partnership. No value or timeline was given for the east-coast build-out. Strategically significant for DP World as cargo diverts from Jebel Ali toward Gulftainer's Khor Fakkan and Fujairah.

title: SOHAR Freezone signs six land-lease deals worth over RO 63m covering 440,000 sqm
summary: At an OPAZ signing ceremony in Muscat, SOHAR Freezone signed six land-lease agreements totalling about 440,000 sqm with announced investment exceeding RO 63m (approx. USD 164m). The largest is the Sohar Automotive & Advanced Industries Park by EW Partners (RO 38m, 317,000 sqm), followed by Voltamp International's transformer plant (RO 15m, 75,000 sqm), Five Star Group textile re-use (RO 3.85m), Lalan Middle East medical devices (RO 1.5m), Volt Power and Lighting (RO 0.8m) and Dynamic Logistics Services (RO 0.15m). The tenants add manufacturing and re-export activity to a zone competing with DP World's Jafza and Jebel Ali for Gulf industrial investment, with Sohar's position outside Hormuz a growing draw.

title: Bénin Terminal (AGL) commissions 22 new Terberg tractors at Port of Cotonou in ~CFA 2bn equipment upgrade
summary: AGL subsidiary Bénin Terminal took delivery of 22 Terberg terminal tractors with trailers, assembled on site at the Port of Cotonou, an investment of nearly CFA 2bn (about EUR 3m) fully self-funded as part of a wider equipment modernisation programme. The 75-tonne tractors lift the handling fleet to 62 machines, with further equipment expected in coming months, aimed at cutting vessel turnaround times. Small in value but shows AGL continuing to invest in its West African container concessions.

title: Tanger Med Zones runs Japan investor roadshow in Osaka and Tokyo with SMBC and Sumitomo
summary: Tanger Med Group held its Japan Roadshow 2026 in Osaka on 9 November (Tokyo session scheduled 12 November), organised with SMBC and Sumitomo Corporation, to attract Japanese automotive, aerospace, electronics, logistics and renewables investors to its ~3,000 ha industrial platform (about 1,500 companies, 145,000 jobs). Tanger Med Zones MD Ahmed Bennis and AMDIE presented Morocco as a gateway to Africa and Europe; no agreements were reported. The push follows the 28 October launch of Tanger Med 3 and signals continued competition with DP World's free-zone offering for Asian manufacturers targeting Europe/Africa.

title: Agility Global Q3 2026: revenue +22% to $1.6bn, Logistics Parks EBIT +58%; Tristar classified as held for sale
summary: Agility Global PLC reported Q3 2026 revenue of USD 1.6bn (+22%) with EBIT roughly flat at USD 125m (controlled businesses +21%) and approved a USD 75m interim dividend. Menzies Aviation revenue rose 22% to USD 974m (EBIT +18% to USD 82m) with G2 integration largely complete; Tristar revenue +24% to USD 419m; Agility Logistics Parks revenue +49% to USD 21m and EBIT +58% to USD 17m, led by new Saudi facilities and higher African occupancy, with a 4.5m sqm land bank (6.1m sqm incl. JVs). Following the 13 October agreement to sell its 65.12% Tristar stake to Aegis Logistics (EV USD 1.5bn, up to USD 581m proceeds, closing by end-March 2027), Tristar is now reported as discontinued operations. DSV stake carried at USD 3.5bn; net debt USD 4.9bn after Saudi land purchases.

title: Cochin Shipyard Q2 FY27: profit halves as shipbuilding slips into loss, ship repair profit more than doubles
summary: Cochin Shipyard's board approved Q2 FY27 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) results on 10 Nov 2026: revenue from operations rose 11.7% YoY to INR 1,249 crore but consolidated net profit fell 50% to INR 53.8 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 4.1%. Shipbuilding (INR 783 crore revenue) swung to an operating loss of INR 6.1 crore versus a INR 150 crore profit a year earlier, while ship repair revenue grew to INR 466 crore with operating profit more than doubling to INR 143 crore. An interim dividend of INR 3/share was declared (record date 16 Nov); the stock fell up to 8% on 11 Nov. Relevant to DP World because Drydocks World is CSL's 50:50 JV partner for the INR 1,800 crore Kochi international ship repair facility, and ship repair is now CSL's profit engine.

title: AD Ports Group posts record Q3 2026 net profit of AED 975m (+64% YoY) on revenue of AED 7.99bn (+48%)
summary: AD Ports Group reported record Q3 2026 results: revenue AED 7.99bn (+48% YoY), EBITDA AED 1.97bn (+63%, margin 24.6%) and net profit AED 975m (+64%; AED 767m attributable, +73%). Maritime & Shipping revenue rose 56% to AED 4.74bn and Logistics 76% to AED 1.96bn, offsetting a 57% YoY fall in UAE container throughput (751k TEU) caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure, which the group mitigated by rerouting feeder and cargo services to Fujairah Terminals and Khor Fakkan plus land/air bridges. KEZAD added 1.2 sq km of net new industrial leases in the quarter (3.2 sq km YTD). The group also confirmed completion of its largest-ever acquisition, Brazil's CLI (closed 1 Oct 2026), and progress on acquiring Germany's MBS Logistics; FCFF was negative AED 691m due to the CLI payment.

title: ICTSI 9M 2026 results: net income up 20% to US$898.9m, volumes up 13% to 12.11m TEU
summary: ICTSI reported first-nine-months 2026 revenue from port operations of US$2.90bn (+24%), EBITDA of US$1.87bn (+21%) and attributable net income of US$898.89m (+20%; US$913.59m / +22% excluding a one-off charge on the Yantai terminal divestment). Volumes rose 13% to 12.11m TEU, driven almost entirely by the newly consolidated Durban Gateway Terminal (South Africa) and Batu Ampar Container Terminal (Indonesia) — organic volume was flat (+0.1%), with Basra Gateway Terminal (Iraq) weak amid regional conflict. EBITDA margin slipped to 64% from 66% on integration costs; Q3 alone: revenue US$984m (+19%), net income US$308.9m (+15%). Full-year capex guidance is US$740m (US$507m spent to date). Signals that ICTSI's growth is now acquisition-led (Durban, Batu Ampar, TLG southern Africa, Brazil agri terminals) rather than organic — directly relevant to DP World's competition for African and emerging-market concessions.

title: Maersk inaugurates 16,000 sqm bonded Semarang Consolidation Centre in Central Java
summary: Maersk inaugurated a new Consolidation Centre in Semarang, Central Java, covering over 16,000 sqm with 15,800 CBM capacity and 11,300 pallet positions on six-level racking, 4 km from the Port of Tanjung Emas and adjacent to Maersk's container depot. The facility operates under a Pusat Logistik Berikat (bonded logistics centre) licence and offers warehousing, consolidation and depot services linked to road, rail and ocean, targeting export manufacturers in footwear, garments and furniture. Maersk now runs more than 128,000 sqm of warehousing across 15 sites in Indonesia, a market where DP World has limited contract-logistics presence.
